title: Maple Sausage Pinwheels
subtitle: Crescent dough spirals with sausage and maple glaze baked golden.
description: Refrigerated crescent dough rolled with seasoned sausage and a touch of maple, sliced into pinwheels and baked until puffed and sticky-sweet. A handheld crowd-pleaser that scales to ten with two sheet pans and minimal active cooking time.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Maple Sausage Pinwheels in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.instruction: Brown sausage, drain well, and mix with cheddar, maple syrup, and black pepper while warm so cheese starts to melt and bind the filling. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roll the dough
steps.instruction: Press crescent dough into two rectangles, sealing seams. Spread sausage filling evenly, roll tight into logs, and pinch seams closed. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Slice pinwheels
steps.instruction: Cut each log into 8–10 pinwheels with a sharp serrated knife. Place cut-side up on parchment-lined sheet pans with space between each spiral. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and bake
steps.instruction: Brush tops with melted butter and maple syrup. Bake at 375°F until golden, puffed, and sausage reaches 165°F in the center. Plan about 18 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Cool slightly and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes so filling sets—hot maple cheese burns tongues. Serve from sheet pans or stack in a warm hotel pan for grab-and-go. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Chill rolled logs 10 minutes before slicing if dough gets soft—clean spirals need a firm log.
Bake both sheet pans on middle and upper racks, swapping halfway for even browning.
Serve with napkins stacked high—these are sticky, handheld, and popular on the way to rigs.
cleanupNotes: Use parchment on sheet pans so maple glaze doesn't weld to the metal during baking.
Soak the sausage mixing bowl immediately—maple and cheese set into a glue once cooled.
leftovers: Reheat pinwheels on a sheet pan at 325°F for 8 minutes until warmed through and crust re-crisp.
Split cold pinwheels and griddle cut-side down with extra maple for a caramelized second-day treat.
